summary: Forty short talks given to disciples at Sawan Ashram after morning meditation, 1967-69. They are mostly about the conditions for the practice (chastity, diary, receptivity, one-pointed attention) and only occasionally about the light itself, but several passages bear on onset: the claim that initiates are given a first experience of light by the teacher's attention and then lose it through dissipation; the staircase image (many steps in darkness, flashes near the roof, full light at the top); the archer who sees only the bird's eye as the model for looking into the middle of what is in front; and the insistence that the single eye opens by receptivity, not by effort. Useful as context for the letters and Q&A volumes; thin on procedure.
why_relevant: Gives the lineage's account of why first light is not seen and of receptivity versus effort; secondary to the letters and Q&A sources.
